Content Tracker + auto-posting with your AI

Two resources that work together. Plan your posts in Notion, and your AI sends them to Buffer.

Content Tracker

Plan it. Make it. Queue it. Keep going.

A ready-to-use Notion content tracker for capturing ideas, moving content through production, preparing finished posts for your Buffer queue, planning content on a calendar, and keeping a searchable library of published content.

Duplicate Content Tracker

Opens the template in Notion. Click Duplicate at the top right to copy it into your own workspace.

Auto-Posting with Your AI

The guide that connects your tracker to Buffer.

Set up Claude or ChatGPT once. Then your AI sends your Ready posts to Buffer for Instagram, TikTok and YouTube, and changes their Status to Queued.

Download the guide (PDF)

Set it up in 4 steps

  1. Duplicate the Content Tracker. Use the button above, then click Duplicate in Notion.
  2. Connect Notion and Buffer to your AI. Step 2 of the guide has the settings for Claude and ChatGPT.
  3. Get one post ready. Delete the example rows, fill in one finished post with its captions and media, and set its Status to Ready.
  4. Send it. Copy the message from Step 5 of the guide to your AI. Check that the post shows up in Buffer and its Status changes to Queued.

How it works

Your AI takes your Ready posts in Publish Order (lowest number first), adds them to your Buffer queue, and marks them Queued. Ask for it any time, or set it to run once a day (Step 6 of the guide).

Status: Idea → Ready → Queued → Published. Mark a post Published once it’s live, or ask your AI to check Buffer and update it.

Keep these field names: Status, Publish Order, Platforms, Instagram Caption, TikTok Caption, YouTube Title, YouTube Description, Media Links. Your AI reads them by name. Everything else in the tracker is yours to change.
